newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Emerging economies show fastest trade growth - WTO.
newsitem.headline: Emerging economies show fastest trade growth - WTO.

text.p: Emerging economies in Asia and Latin America have generally been the fastest growing traders on the global scene in the 1990s, the World Trade Organisation (WTO) reported on Thursday.

But Poland, the only former communist transition economy to figure, was the second fastest growing importer, while European Union member Ireland also made it into the top 10 in the dynamic exporters' league.

In its annual survey of global trade performance, the WTO said that between 1990 and 1996 Malaysia topped the exporters table with an annual average growth rate of 18 percent, based on U.S. dollar values.

Most dynamic importer was Argentina, which returned a whopping annual average growth of 34 percent, well ahead of Poland with 22 percent and Malaysia which matched its exports figure of 18 percent with its imports.
Argentina's import trade, WTO analysts said, was largely due to the implementation of the Mercosur trade agreement linking it with Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Brazil also benefited, coming equal fifth in the import league with an annual average growth rate of 17 percent.
In Asia, the Philippines and China also turned in good performances for both exports and imports.

WTO chief economist Richard Blackhurt told a news briefing that the tables reflected a surge of economic reform -- by the Asians in he late 1980s and by the Latin Americans a little later in the early 1990s.
"We can see the effects of trade reform and deregulation on performance," he said.
In second place to Malaysia among exporters, the Philippines recorded an annual average growth of 17 percent over the period, and China, in third place equal with Thailand, hit 16 percent.
Singapore was fifth together with Mexico at 15 percent, Ireland at seventh with 13 percent, followed by Kuwait, South Korea, Indonesia and Argentina, all on 12 percent.

Ireland's performance, which put it alone among developed economies among the top 10 in either import or export leagues, was largely due to a boom in sales of its high technology office and telecommunications equipment, Blackhurst said.
Among importers, the Philippines was fourth with 18 percent ahead of China and Brazil on 17 percent, and Colombia on seventh place with 16 percent.

Eighth most dynamic importers were the United Arab Emirates and Chile, both with growth rates of 15 percent, while Mexico, Singapore and South Korea were equal 10th with an annual average of 14 percent growth.
